overview: Midea Real Estate was, through 2023, a large Foshan-based Chinese residential property developer (FY2023 revenue RMB73.6bn, total assets RMB201.6bn). On 22 October 2024 it completed a 'distribution in specie' that spun off and transferred the entire heavy-asset property-development-and-sales (PD&S) business to its controlling shareholders (the He Xiangjian/Lu Deyan family, who also control Midea Group, the appliance maker, as a separate related entity) via a new private vehicle, Midea Construction (BVI) Limited, with shareholders offered one Midea Construction share or a HK$5.90 cash alternative per 3990.HK share held. What remains listed as 3990.HK is a far smaller, asset-light services group operating under four segments: project/development management services, property management services, asset operation (commercial properties and industrial parks), and real estate technology. Post-spinoff total assets fell from RMB201.6bn to RMB9.7bn and revenue fell from RMB73.6bn to RMB3.7bn (FY2024), with the business still based in Foshan, Guangdong and operating almost entirely within mainland China.

structural_event.event: Distribution in specie and disposal of the property development and sales (PD&S) business
structural_event.mechanics: Midea Real Estate transferred its core heavy-asset residential development business to a newly formed BVI vehicle, Midea Construction (BVI) Limited, which was distributed to shareholders (1 Midea Construction share per 1 3990.HK share), with a cash alternative of HK$5.90/share offered by the controlling shareholders who took up the distributed shares themselves (effectively privatising the PD&S business under the controlling family outside the listed structure).
structural_event.rationale_disclosed: Management (Chairman's Statement) cited the need to reduce debt and credit risk associated with the heavy-asset, highly-levered nature of property development amid a prolonged industry downturn, and to reposition the listed entity around 'light-asset' services across the real estate value chain (project management, property management, asset operation, real estate technology) that generate recurring service fees rather than cyclical, capital-intensive development profit.

financial_effect.fy2024_discontinued_loss: approximately -RMB2,058 million (loss from the business transferred out, reflected as a one-off loss on distribution/disposal of discontinued operations)

structural_event.note: FY2023 balance sheet was not restated for comparability; reported FY2023 vs FY2024 balance sheet figures are not like-for-like. All figures from FY2024 onward reflect the continuing, post-spinoff entity only.

business_model.summary: Midea RE is now an asset-light, fee-based real estate services platform. It earns development/project management fees (overseeing construction and sales of real estate projects, including those now held by its former parent/controlling shareholder as well as third parties), recurring property management fees (residential, industrial park, healthcare/elderly-care, school, and commercial-office management), asset operation income (shopping malls, long-term rental apartments, office buildings, industrial park leasing under the 'Yueran/Wonderful' brand), and real estate technology revenue (modular/prefabricated construction (MiC), interior fit-out systems, smart-home products via its REMAC ASPACE unit). Revenue is a mix of recurring, contracted service fees (property management, asset operation) and more project/transaction-based fees (project management, real estate technology) that are more cyclical and tied to new construction and sales volumes.

revenue_streams.name: Property Management Services
revenue_streams.description: Residential, industrial park, healthcare/elderly-care, school and commercial-office property management; contracted GFA ~95.5m sqm, under-management ~84m sqm as of H1 2026. Core, most recurring revenue stream.

revenue_streams.name: Asset Operation
revenue_streams.description: Commercial property leasing (shopping malls under 'Yueran Square/Block' brands, long-term rental apartments, offices) and industrial park leasing/factory delivery. H1 2026 revenue +103% YoY on industrial park factory deliveries; flagship Foshan mall now mature with ~74% NOI margin.

revenue_streams.name: Project Management Services
revenue_streams.description: Full-chain development management (design, construction management, sales management) for real estate projects, now mostly for assets held by the controlling shareholder post-restructuring, plus emerging third-party clients. H1 2026 revenue -34.7% YoY on lower property sales and managed GFA.

revenue_streams.name: Real Estate Technology
revenue_streams.description: REMAC ASPACE: modular integrated construction (MiC), prefabricated concrete components, smart-home/interior systems. Pivoting from mainland PC-component market (shrinking) toward Hong Kong and overseas developed markets. H1 2026 revenue -71.6% YoY, reflecting lumpy, contract-driven recognition.

business_model.customer_type: Mixed B2B/B2B2C: controlling shareholder and its affiliates (connected-party project management and construction-materials transactions under renewed framework agreements through December 2026), third-party property developers, residential property owners/homeowners' associations, industrial park tenants, and institutional/government clients (hospitals, schools).
business_model.geographic_mix: Almost entirely mainland China, concentrated in Guangdong (Foshan/Shunde home base) with expansion into Wuxi, Xuzhou, Guiyang, Zhuzhou, Handan, Zhenjiang; REMAC ASPACE has early-stage exposure to Hong Kong and is exploring overseas developed markets for modular construction.

main_competitors: China Resources Mixc Lifestyle (property management/commercial operation)
Other mid-tier Chinese property management and construction-management firms (CRIC/CPMRI Top 20-100 rankings)
competitive_position.market_position: A mid-tier player (ranked roughly Top 16-22 by comprehensive strength among Chinese property service companies in industry rankings cited by the company) with a much smaller scale than the leading developer-affiliated property managers (China Resources Mixc, Country Garden Services, Onewo) following the 2024 restructuring. No longer competes as a top-tier developer; now competes as a smaller asset-light services provider leveraging its former parent/controlling-shareholder relationship.

moat_factors.description: Guaranteed recurring base of project and property management mandates from the controlling shareholder's (ex-Midea RE) development pipeline and existing managed GFA, via renewed connected-transaction framework agreements (through Dec 2026), providing revenue visibility third-party-only competitors lack.

'Midea' brand name and manufacturing heritage (quality/craftsmanship positioning) differentiate marketing, though the listed entity is legally and economically distinct from Midea Group (the global appliance maker) despite shared family ownership.

Differentiated expansion into non-residential property management niches — hospitals/healthcare and elderly care (e.g., Heyou International Hospital), industrial parks — where competition is less commoditized than standard residential management.
REMAC ASPACE's MiC modular construction has Hong Kong Buildings Department IPA certification (unusual among peers) but remains small-scale and loss-prone as the mainland PC-component market shrinks.
Gearing fell from 75% to ~43-48% and the group shed most interest-bearing debt tied to the development business, giving balance-sheet flexibility relative to still-distressed peers.

weaknesses: Heavy reliance on the controlling shareholder/connected parties for a meaningful share of project management and construction-related revenue — not a fully independent, arm's-length services business
Much smaller scale than top-tier property managers post-spinoff, limiting pricing power and ability to win large third-party mandates
Project management and real estate technology segments are volatile/declining (down 34.7% and 71.6% YoY respectively in H1 2026), indicating the 'growth' segments are not yet proven at scale
Managed GFA growth depends on the controlling shareholder's own (much smaller, post-spinoff) development pipeline delivering new projects on schedule
Historical association with China's troubled property sector may continue to weigh on investor perception and valuation multiples even though the balance-sheet risk has been shed

growth_drivers: Expansion of property management into higher-margin, less-penetrated non-residential verticals: industrial parks, healthcare/elderly-care facilities, schools

Third-party project management expansion beyond the controlling shareholder's pipeline, leveraging brand and track record (e.g., Wuxi Midea Dongwangfu project, Xuzhou Midea Junlanyue 'ready-built-home' sales strategy)

Asset operation scale-up: new self-owned and light-asset (third-party operated) commercial/industrial park projects (e.g., Shunbei Ruichuang Intelligent Manufacturing Park, Beijiao Vitality Island), maturing malls lifting portfolio-average NOI margin
REMAC ASPACE's pivot from the oversupplied mainland prefabricated-concrete market toward Hong Kong and overseas developed markets for modular/MiC construction
Continued deleveraging and shift to recurring, contracted service-fee income reducing cyclicality versus the pre-spinoff developer model
Potential consolidation/market-share gains as weaker, more indebted property-service peers (tied to distressed developer parents) exit or shrink amid the broader sector shakeout

business.description: A significant share of project management and construction-materials-linked revenue flows through continuing connected transactions with the controlling shareholder's (spun-off) development business; any slowdown in that affiliate's project launches directly hits Midea RE's project management revenue, as seen in H1 2026 (-34.7% YoY).
Post-spinoff, Midea RE lacks the scale of China Resources Mixc, Country Garden Services or Onewo in winning large, competitively-bid third-party property/asset management contracts.
REMAC ASPACE revenue is small, lumpy, and highly volatile (down >70% YoY in H1 2026) as it exits the shrinking domestic PC-component market before overseas/Hong Kong contracts scale.
Public market may continue to discount the stock for its origin as (and residual brand ties to) a Chinese property developer despite the 2024 clean-out of development assets and liabilities.

financial.description: Cash and bank deposits fell from RMB1,646.4m (FY2025) to RMB1,169.7m (H1 2026, -29% in six months), partly reflecting dividend payments and short-term borrowing paydown; sustained cash burn would constrain the capital-return policy.

The company pays interim and final dividends (e.g., HK$0.12 interim, HK$0.19 final disclosed in FY2025/2026 reports) funded from a much smaller earnings base (~RMB255-305m attributable profit per half); payout ratio pressure could emerge if project management/real estate technology declines continue.
Long-term borrowings fell to zero by end-FY2025 from RMB586.6m in FY2024, reducing refinancing risk, but short-term borrowings remain variable (RMB591.9m at FY2025 vs RMB48.8m at FY2024).

regulatory.description: Ongoing continuing connected transactions with the controlling shareholder (property management and construction framework agreements renewed through December 2026) require HKEX Listing Rule disclosure/annual review and cap compliance; breach or unfavorable renewal terms could affect revenue or governance perception.

While no longer a developer itself, Midea RE's fee income is indirectly tied to the health of China's property sector (new project launches, sales velocity, developer solvency) and therefore to government stimulus/regulatory policy toward the sector.

macro.description: Management describes the market as in an 'L-shaped bottoming' cycle with weak recovery and structural divergence between core and lower-tier cities; a prolonged downturn suppresses new project launches, sales-linked management fees, and demand for commercial/industrial space.
Asset operation (malls, offices, rental apartments) revenue is sensitive to local consumer spending and corporate demand for office/industrial space in China's affected secondary cities.

macro.risk: RMB currency exposure for overseas (HK/export) ambitions
macro.description: As REMAC ASPACE and other segments pursue Hong Kong/overseas contracts, RMB/HKD or RMB/USD movements become a modest incremental factor.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: China's residential property sector remains in a multi-year structural downturn/bottoming process; property management and asset-light services are viewed as relatively more resilient sub-sectors, but still indirectly exposed to developer health, new-project launch volumes, and local government stimulus measures. Property management industry consolidation is ongoing as developer-affiliated managers tied to distressed parents are repriced or restructured.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate. Property management and asset operation provide more stable, contracted recurring revenue; project management and real estate technology remain cyclical and tied to new construction/sales activity.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low-to-moderate direct exposure given minimal long-term debt post-spinoff; indirect sensitivity through the broader property sector's response to PBOC rate/mortgage policy, which drives developer activity and thus Midea RE's project management and real estate technology demand.
key_input_costs: Labor costs for property management services
Leasing/occupancy costs for owned commercial assets

recent_developments.event: Completed the distribution in specie and disposal of the property development and sales business to Midea Construction (BVI) Limited, held by the controlling shareholders, transforming Midea RE into a light-asset services group.

'Project management services' established as a new reporting segment, handling full-chain development management for the controlling shareholder's and third parties' real estate projects post-restructuring.

FY2025 revenue RMB4,149.1m (+11.4% YoY), net profit to owners RMB559.3m (+16.9% YoY), gearing stable at 47.7%; short-term borrowings rose sharply from RMB48.8m to RMB591.9m while long-term borrowings were eliminated.

Revenue declined 5.7% YoY to RMB1,882.5m and net profit to owners fell 16.7% YoY to RMB254.6m, driven by a 34.7% drop in project management revenue and a 71.6% drop in real estate technology revenue, partly offset by asset operation revenue more than doubling (+103.2% YoY) on industrial park factory deliveries; gross margin improved to 33.5% from 30.8%.

Board/management changes: Wang Dazai redesignated Co-Chairman and President (Oct 2025) then sole Chairman and President (by mid-2026 interim report); new executive director She Zuojun appointed July 2026, replacing Hao Hengle who resigned June 2026.

Expansion into new niches: entry into healthcare/elderly-care property management (Heyou International Hospital, Shenzhen Zhongshan Obstetrics and Gynecology Hospital), new light-asset industrial park third-party operation wins (Shunbei Ruichuang Intelligent Manufacturing Park), and new commercial concept launches (Beijiao Vitality Island).

Stock price declined materially through 2026 (reports show roughly 44-52% drawdown year-to-date/one-year as of September 2026), with trailing P/E in the low-to-mid single digits (~5-6x), reflecting market skepticism about the scale and durability of the post-spinoff services business despite continued profitability.

guidance.as_of: H1 2026 interim results (announced 10 August 2026) and FY2025 annual report (announced 31 March 2026)

items.target: Steady coordinated development of four segments: project management, property management, asset operation, real estate technology
items.notes: No specific quantitative revenue or margin targets disclosed; guidance is qualitative, emphasizing third-party expansion in project management, consolidation of residential property management base plus expansion into industrial parks/healthcare, disciplined asset operation expansion in core cities, and technology-driven product differentiation.

items.target: Interim dividend HK$0.12/share (H1 2026); Final dividend HK$0.19/share (FY2025)
items.vs_prior: not explicitly compared; payout maintained despite lower H1 2026 earnings
items.notes: Company has continued to pay interim and final dividends post-spinoff; no explicit multi-year payout ratio policy disclosed in extracted filings.

items.target: Continue deleveraging and light-asset, low-leverage, stable cash flow model
items.notes: Gearing ratio fell from 75.1% (FY2023, pre-spinoff) to 47.7% (FY2024/FY2025) to 43.3% (H1 2026); long-term borrowings eliminated by FY2025.

guidance.management_commentary: Management (H1 2026 MD&A) characterizes the China property market as in an 'L-shaped bottoming, weak recovery, structurally divergent' cycle with core cities recovering ahead of lower-tier cities, and states that the light-asset business model's competitive advantages 'have become increasingly evident' as the Group shifts from incremental development profit to recurring operating service fees. No formal numeric revenue/earnings guidance for FY2026 was found in the extracted filings; commentary is directional/strategic rather than target-based.

bull_case: Clean balance-sheet reset: shed ~RMB190bn of assets and the associated debt/credit risk of heavy-asset development, cutting gearing from 75% to under 45% and eliminating long-term borrowings, materially de-risking the equity story versus peers still carrying developer balance sheets

Now a recurring-fee, asset-light services business (property management ~48% of revenue, asset operation ~30%) that is structurally less cyclical than its former development-profit model, with still-growing managed GFA (~84m sqm) and improving asset-operation occupancy (94% vs 91% YoY)

Low valuation (trailing P/E in the ~5-6x range per third-party data) may not fully reflect the de-risked, dividend-paying, profitable nature of the post-spinoff entity if the market is still pricing it on legacy-developer multiples
Diversification into non-residential property management niches (healthcare, industrial parks, schools) where competition is less commoditized offers a higher-margin growth runway

Continued financial backing/pipeline support from the controlling shareholder via renewed connected-transaction agreements (through Dec 2026) provides revenue visibility unusual for an independent services firm of this size
bear_case: Heavy dependence on the controlling shareholder's own (much smaller) development pipeline for project management revenue, which fell 34.7% YoY in H1 2026 as that pipeline shrinks — the 'growth' segment is structurally capped by an affiliate's reduced build-out, not by Midea RE's own market execution

Real estate technology (REMAC ASPACE) revenue collapsed 71.6% YoY in H1 2026 and remains unproven at scale outside the shrinking mainland PC-component market, undermining the 'four-pillar' growth narrative

Scale disadvantage versus top-tier property managers (China Resources Mixc, Onewo, Country Garden Services) limits ability to win large competitively-bid third-party mandates, keeping the company a mid-tier, largely domestically-concentrated player

Overall group net profit and revenue declined YoY in H1 2026 (-16.7% and -5.7% respectively) even after the spinoff, showing the post-restructuring entity is not immune to China's weak property-sector demand environment

Deep 2026 share-price drawdown (reportedly 44-52% YoY as of September 2026) despite continued profitability suggests persistent market skepticism about the durability, scale, and independence of the post-spinoff business model from its controlling family's broader property interests
